image_prompt: A young German nobleman in his twenties from 18th century Anhalt-Zerbst, physically unremarkable with an air of mediocrity about him. Slender to average build, pallid complexion typical of northern European aristocracy. Light brown or sandy hair styled in a modest powdered wig with side curls, less elaborate than fashionable nobility. Wearing a military-style coat in muted Prussian colors - dark navy or charcoal gray with minimal embellishment, brass buttons dulled with age, showing the restrained poverty of minor German princes. Simple white stock tie at the neck, slightly disheveled. Facial features are ordinary, almost forgettable - a weak chin, slightly prominent nose, thin lips set in an uncertain expression that wavers between petulance and nervous anxiety. Eyes are restless, pale blue or gray, conveying instability and eccentricity. Narrow shoulders slightly hunched, suggesting both physical weakness and the burden of unwanted expectations. Overall appearance communicates faded nobility, provincial obscurity, and inherited peculiarity - a last remnant of declining aristocratic lineage.
